disasters.summary: Tropical Cyclone Arnab made landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast in India early on 28 October 2026, after it began on 25 October. The India Meteorological Department said heavy rain and strong winds would continue in coastal Andhra Pradesh and parts of southern Odisha. Reports on deaths conflict; the government reported none, while some outlets reported three. The status as of 28 October is ongoing for rain and wind effects.

disasters.summary: Tropical Cyclone Champi, known as Super Typhoon Rosal in the Philippines, began on 14 October 2026 and affected Taiwan, Okinawa in Japan, Shanghai in China, and Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands. It became extratropical on 25 October and dissipated on 27 October, according to Wikipedia. Direct effects were still reported on 26 October, when heavy rain was forecast for parts of Japan. No source gives the status as of 29 October.

disasters.summary: Drought in East Africa and the Central Sahel began on 21 May 2026 and is ongoing as of 29 October 2026, according to the latest report found, dated 25 October. A US forecast cited in that report says the El Niño driving the drought may last into early 2027. No official end of the event has been declared. Reported impacts include cropland damage in Ethiopia and famine risk in Sudan, where drought is compounded by conflict.

disasters.summary: Prolonged drought is affecting parts of Central America, which began on 21 April 2026. On 24 October 2026 the IFRC said about one million people in Honduras are affected. A red alert covers 103 Honduran municipalities, and 234 more are under other alert levels. Drought is projected to worsen between October 2026 and March 2027. Western Nicaragua and southeastern Mexico also report dry conditions.

disasters.summary: Drought has affected crops, river levels and water supply across much of Europe in 2026. A JRC bulletin dated 23 October 2026 reported persistently low soil moisture in western, central and south-eastern Europe, hampering rapeseed emergence. The sources do not confirm the 21 December 2025 start date. Reported losses include $3.6bn in agricultural losses and a French corn harvest 35% below 2025.

disasters.summary: Hurricane Vance, a cyclone that started on 21 October 2026, is now a weakening tropical storm offshore from Mexico's Pacific coast, according to the National Hurricane Center bulletin issued 27 October 2026 at 08:00 MST. It has 35-knot winds and is expected to turn north toward the entrance of the Gulf of California by Thursday. No land impacts have been reported. Mexican authorities have taken preventive measures in five Pacific states.

disasters.summary: A magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck near Khuzdar in Balochistan, Pakistan, on 17 October 2026 at about 10:07 am local time. USGS placed the epicentre about 48 km west-northwest of Khuzdar at a depth of about 10 km; Pakistan's PMD gave magnitude 5.9 at 25 km depth. One death was reported on 18 October after a rock fell in the Naal area, and several mud houses were damaged. No reports dated after 18 October were found.

disasters.summary: Taal Volcano in Batangas, Philippines, began erupting on 8 October 2026, with phreatomagmatic eruptions and tremor continuing at low level since then. PHIVOLCS kept Alert Level 1 after a minor eruption on 22 October that sent a plume 1,200 meters above the main crater. More than 100 Agoncillo residents were evacuated after the first eruption. The notes found no later evacuation status.

disasters.summary: A flash flood struck Rasuwa district in Nepal on 26 August 2026, reportedly linked to a suspected glacial lake outburst or high-altitude outburst event; the cause is not settled. Places along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli corridor were damaged, and deaths and missing people were reported in early counts. As of 11 October 2026, relief and recovery were ongoing, with two centres across the Trishuli River still inaccessible.

No later source was found on the current status.

disasters.summary: Heavy monsoon rain and runoff from upstream hills flooded much of Cox's Bazar district in south-eastern Bangladesh from 5 July 2026. Parts of Chattogram, Bandarban and other districts were also affected. IFRC's DREF operation, started 14 July 2026, runs to 31 January 2027. By late August 2026, no monitored river station was above danger level, and the response had moved to damage assessment and recovery.
